Text to type: A latte, or caffe latte, comes from Italy. It is made with espresso and steamed milk. A latte does not have the same thick foam layer as a cappuccino. It is also larger. A cappuccino can come in a small 140 ml cup with thick foam. A caffe latte can come in a larger 230 ml glass or cup. Traditionally, it is served in a glass. In Italian, latte means milk. In English, latte means the coffee drink. These details can help you choose between the two drinks.

Reading

Part 1: A Place for Drinks and Talk

A cafe is a place that serves coffee drinks.

A coffeehouse is another name for a cafe.

The drinks can include espresso, latte, americano, and cappuccino.

Some cafes also serve light snacks.

People use cafes in different ways.

Friends can meet and talk there.

A person can also sit alone and pass the time.

This social side is important.

You are not only buying a drink.

You are entering a place where a short, friendly talk can feel natural.

Reading

Part 2: Espresso as the Base

Espresso comes from Italy.

It is a concentrated form of coffee.

Hot water moves under high pressure through finely ground coffee beans.

A typical serving is small, about 25 to 30 ml.

An espresso has a dark body.

A lighter foam sits on top.

This foam is called crema.

Espresso is also the base for other drinks.

Cappuccino and caffe latte both begin with espresso.

Knowing this helps you understand the drinks on a cafe menu.

Reading

Part 3: Cappuccino and Its Foam

A cappuccino is an espresso-based drink.

It has espresso and steamed milk.

Steamed milk is milk heated with steam for a coffee drink.

Foamed milk goes on top.

The top layer is thick foam.

This gives a cappuccino a clear look and feel.

Today, it usually has one espresso shot, but it can also have a double or triple shot.

A cappuccino is typically smaller than a caffe latte.

Think of espresso below, warm milk in the middle, and thick foam above.

Reading

Part 4: Latte and More Milk

A latte, or caffe latte, comes from Italy.

It is made with espresso and steamed milk.

A latte does not have the same thick foam layer as a cappuccino.

It is also larger.

A cappuccino can come in a small 140 ml cup with thick foam.

A caffe latte can come in a larger 230 ml glass or cup.

Traditionally, it is served in a glass.

In Italian, latte means milk.

In English, latte means the coffee drink.

These details can help you choose between the two drinks.

Reading

Part 5: Making a Clear Order

The customer names the drink in a short order.

I would like an espresso, please.

A cappuccino, please.

A latte, please.

Please keeps the order polite.

Thank you comes after the cafe worker brings the drink.

The drink name, please, and thanks are enough.

Reading

Part 6: Adding Small Talk

A cafe is a place to meet and talk.

Small talk is light friendly talk after the order, not the drink name.

This place is busy today.

That line notices the room.

It is short and friendly.

The other person may answer with a few words.

Then the talk can stop.
